author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
summary: A leader's emotional self-control is a built discipline, not a fixed temperament, and it sets the operating climate for everyone around them. Composure is a deliberate practice that compounds into team trust.
usable_principle: Treat emotional steadiness as a trainable operating discipline. Your composure sets the climate; manage it deliberately on set and in client work.
sniped_relevance: SNIPED on-set energy management (the posing system already says affirm early, never go silent). BASEPLATE client steadiness under pressure.

source_title: Team of Rivals · Surround With Abler Dissent
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
concept: Security with rivals beats comfort with loyalists
summary: Surrounding yourself with abler, dissenting talent is a confidence signal, not a risk. Security with rivals outperforms comfort with yes-people, because dissent surfaces what loyalty hides.
usable_principle: Hire and consult people abler than you and invite dissent. Comfort with loyalists hides risk; security with rivals exposes it.
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE team and advisor selection. Tempers the solo-operator instinct to avoid challenge.

source_title: Team of Rivals · Absorb Blame, Distribute Credit
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
concept: Direction of blame and credit builds trust
summary: Absorb blame downward and distribute credit outward to build durable team trust. The direction blame and credit flow is a deliberate leadership lever, not an afterthought.
usable_principle: Absorb blame downward, push credit outward. The flow of blame and credit is a trust-building lever you control.
sniped_relevance: SNIPED assistant and collaborator relationships. BASEPLATE partnership and subcontractor trust.

source_title: Leadership in Turbulent Times · Match Mode to Moment
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
concept: Diagnose what the moment requires first
summary: Before choosing how to operate, diagnose what the moment requires. Four separable operating postures exist (transformational, crisis-management, turnaround, visionary), each with its own decision pattern. Match the mode to the situation rather than running one fixed style.
usable_principle: Diagnose the moment, then pick the operating posture (transformational, crisis, turnaround, visionary) it requires, instead of running one default style.
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE and SNIPED phase transitions: the lean build phase, a client crisis, a turnaround, and a vision push each call for a different posture.

source_title: Leadership in Turbulent Times · Capacity Is Built
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
concept: Operator capacity is forged, not innate
summary: Leadership and operator capacity is a built skill forged through adversity, not an innate trait. Treat founder development as deliberate practice, expecting the hardest periods to be where capacity is made.
usable_principle: Treat your own operator development as deliberate practice. Capacity is forged in the hard periods; do not read difficulty as disqualification.
sniped_relevance: Directly relevant to BJ's solo-operator phase and the repetition-over-novelty doctrine. Frames the grind as capacity-building.

source_title: Dichotomy of Leadership · Calibration Between Opposites
author: Jocko Willink, Leif Babin
concept: Most failure is one true principle taken too far
summary: Leadership is calibration between opposing forces, not fixed maxims. Most failures come from taking one true principle too far: too aggressive or too cautious, too rigid or too loose. The skill is balancing the dichotomy for the situation.
usable_principle: Lead by calibrating opposites, not by maxims. When something fails, check whether you took one good principle too far, and rebalance.
sniped_relevance: SNIPED and BASEPLATE operating decisions: discipline vs adaptability, owning everything vs empowering, holding the floor vs flexing.

source_title: Dichotomy of Leadership · Own Everything Yet Empower
author: Jocko Willink, Leif Babin
summary: Own everything in your world while empowering others to act. For a solo operator the live question is what to keep under direct ownership versus what to delegate, holding accountability without becoming the bottleneck.
usable_principle: Own the outcome, delegate the execution. Decide deliberately what stays under your direct ownership and what you empower others to run.
sniped_relevance: The SNIPED assistant/retoucher delegation boundary and the lean-override hour budget. Pairs with the effective-hourly-wage test.

source_title: Dichotomy of Leadership · Discipline vs Rigidity
author: Jocko Willink, Leif Babin
summary: Hold standards and cadence firmly while staying adaptive when conditions change. Discipline that hardens into rigidity fails; the goal is firm structure with situational flex.
usable_principle: Design operating cadence to be firm but not rigid: hold the standards and the rhythm, flex the tactics when conditions change.
sniped_relevance: The OS execution discipline (Monday cockpit, recurring checklists) plus the room to adapt per situation.

author: Charlie Munger (via framework)
concept: Run every call through rational and psychological tracks
summary: Run every high-stakes decision through two tracks: a rational track using multidisciplinary mental models, and a psychological track auditing the biases that may be distorting judgment. Add inversion as a standing step: ask how it fails.
usable_principle: Two-track every big decision: the rational model track and the bias-audit track, with inversion (how does this fail) as a required step.
sniped_relevance: Supplements the single existing chunk. The OS decision-memo and challenge skills can adopt the explicit two-track structure.

author: Tetlock / Good Judgment (via framework)
concept: Triage by tractability, then Fermi-ize and use the outside view
summary: Triage questions by tractability before spending effort (clocklike use heuristics, Goldilocks use the full method, cloud-like stay near base rate and do not over-invest). Then Fermi-ize, anchor on the outside-view base rate, and update incrementally.
usable_principle: Forecast in order: triage by tractability, decompose (Fermi), anchor on the base rate, then update in small diagnostic steps.
sniped_relevance: Pairs with the decision-systems base-rate and EV chunks. Useful for any SNIPED/BASEPLATE go/no-go forecast.

author: Hamilton Helmer (via framework)
concept: Seven sources of Power and the 3 S filter
summary: Assess strategic position against the seven sources of Power (scale, network, counter-positioning, switching costs, branding, cornered resource, process), and apply the 3 S filter: an advantage is Power only if it is Superior, Significant, and Sustainable, judged competitor by competitor.
usable_principle: Test any claimed moat against the seven Powers and the 3 S filter (superior, significant, sustainable), per competitor, not as a single global score.
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE and SNIPED moat analysis. The lineage doctrine and Direction Stack are candidate cornered-resource/branding powers; test them honestly.

author: Richard Rumelt (via framework)
summary: Every real strategy has a kernel: a diagnosis naming the critical challenge, a guiding policy giving direction with explicit trade-offs, and coordinated action. Generate at least three alternative diagnoses before committing, since each framing implies a different policy.
usable_principle: Build strategy as a kernel: name the real challenge, set a guiding policy with trade-offs, coordinate action. Reframe the diagnosis at least three ways first.
sniped_relevance: Replaces vision-statement drift in SNIPED/BASEPLATE planning. The anomaly heuristic (where facts defy received wisdom) is the edge-finder.
